### 🧪 NetSpeedTray 2.2.0-rc.2

rc.2 was supposed to be a small follow-up. Then I decided 2.2.0 should stay Latest for a good while, so everything still open went in first: known bugs, promises and the smaller feature requests. It's a bigger rc than planned, so it needs your eyes.

**Prereleases don't update in-app, and WinGet and the Store won't offer this one.** Download Setup.exe or the portable zip below and install over rc.1, any beta or 2.1.7. If you're on rc.1 or a beta, the running app closes itself and comes back. Your history and settings carry over.

### What's new since rc.1

- **Dark and light taskbar colors** that follow Windows mode, a **Medium** level for color coding, and **your own mini graph colors**. Thanks @Angel-Informatico (#332), @2g4b (#9) and @thefaboss (#117).
- **A more readable widget.** Text stays clear over the mini graph, High/Medium/Low stay apart with red-green color blindness, and High Contrast and accent-colored taskbars work. It also uses the clock's font now, Segoe UI Variable.
- **Show on all taskbars:** a copy of the widget on every monitor's taskbar. Settings → Widget, off by default. Thanks @dovletix (#229).
- **The widget steps aside when your app buttons reach it** on a horizontal Windows 11 taskbar, and comes back when there's room. On by default (Settings → Widget). Thanks @relu616 (#24).
- **Side taskbars:** the widget keeps clear of app buttons as apps come and go, not just at startup.
- **Start NetSpeedTray again to bring a lost widget back.** No more Task Manager. Thanks @VenusGirl (#234).
- **Usage by day, month and year** behind the Overview's usage card, with CSV export, and **Back up history** in Settings → Advanced. Thanks @Falenone (#334).
- **LibreHardwareMonitor with a password and a custom port**, a **GPU picker** for PCs with two GPUs (thanks @balciseri, #236), and **°C or °F**.
- **Check connection shows your IP addresses and DNS servers.** Thanks @CMTriX (#214).
- The Monitor's network graph shows gaps where nothing was measured, its axes show your unit, and hovering reads real samples.
- An IT policy to turn update checks off, and a new [DEPLOYING.md](https://github.com/erez-c137/NetSpeedTray/blob/main/DEPLOYING.md).
- **Windows 10:** the widget no longer blinks out when you maximize and restore windows (thanks @pasharm), and it should stay clear of the taskbar's Desktop/Links toolbars (thanks @Achaean, #324 - untested on Windows 10 so far).
- Plenty of fixes: the update check works on a fresh Windows install (2.1.7 failed there with a certificate error), Check connection says "No connection" when the cable or Wi-Fi drops, changing the display scale no longer leaves the widget the wrong size until a restart, it doesn't float in a corner during an Explorer restart, full-screen Remote Desktop on several monitors hides it (#132), and more. Hungarian, Turkish and German updates, thanks @cscsanaki, @lezgintekay and @emgeka.

### Heads up

- **The default High/Medium/Low colors and the font changed.** Colors and fonts you picked yourself are kept.
- **Threshold boxes now show your unit.** They always worked in Mbps even when they said MB/s, so a "5" you typed under MB/s now reads "0.625 MB/s". Your colors don't change; type it again if you meant 5 MB/s.
- **If you followed rc.1's LibreHardwareMonitor hint**, check that port 8085 isn't open in your firewall. The new hint explains.
- **If you dragged the widget on a side taskbar before**, right-click it → Reset Position once so it can find a free spot by itself.

### What I'd love you to test

- **Side taskbars + app buttons:** open and close a lot of apps. Does the widget stay clear? On a horizontal Windows 11 taskbar, does it step aside and come back cleanly?
- **Show on all taskbars, with two or more monitors:** do the copies sit right on each taskbar, at different scaling and on a side taskbar too? Unplug a monitor, restart Explorer - do they come back?
- **The new colors** on dark, light, accent-colored and High Contrast taskbars. Turn on Medium and run a speed test - can you tell the three apart and read the text over the graph?
- **Usage by day:** does today's row match the card? Try **Back up history** and open the copy.
- **LibreHardwareMonitor with authentication on:** enter the password in Settings → Hardware. Do temperatures come back?
- **Change the display scale** while the app runs. Does the widget fit the taskbar within a few seconds?
- **Pull the cable or turn off Wi-Fi** with the Monitor open. Does the pill say "Router: No connection", and recover when you reconnect?
- **Lose the widget, then start NetSpeedTray again.** Does it come back? **Two GPUs?** Try the picker in Settings → Hardware.

### What's next

If this one's quiet for about a week, it ships as 2.2.0 through the in-app updater, WinGet and the Store. Lots of new strings this time, listed for translators in #364.

Found something? Comment on #373 with a support bundle (Export support bundle at the bottom of Settings). Usernames, paths and IPs are stripped from it.
